title: Mega Man 11
intro: A route through the Robot Masters, the utility items worth collecting, and the final stages. Read the introduction for the controls and systems specific to this game.
facts: Weapons, utility items and final stages
primer: Mega Man 11 restores the slide and charged Buster. Speed Gear slows the world so you can read hazards; Power Gear strengthens the Buster and special weapons. Both build heat, so switch them off before overheating.

At low health, Double Gear activates both together for a short emergency burst. It cannot be cancelled and leaves you with a recovery period. Use it deliberately, rather than waiting until a hit is already unavoidable.

There are no hidden armor parts or permanent health tanks. Dr. Light’s shop sells reusable parts and consumable E/W/M-Tanks. Rush Coil is available from the start; Rush Jet unlocks after four Robot Master clears. Purchased parts can be enabled or disabled in the menu.
routeIntro: Block is a practical starting point for learning the gears. Follow the weakness chain through Acid → Impact → Bounce → Fuse → Tundra → Torch → Blast.

stages.name: Block Man
stages.tip: Use charged Buster first. During his giant form, use Speed Gear to cross safely and target the glowing chest.

stages.name: Acid Man
stages.tip: Drop blocks to break his shield, then attack before he reforms it. Acid pools can change when enemies fire into them.

stages.name: Impact Man
stages.tip: Raise Acid Barrier and fire at openings; use Speed Gear to read the drill charges.

stages.name: Bounce Man
stages.tip: Pile Driver splits his body. Keep track of the central piece and avoid the bouncing hands.

items.name: Rush Jet
items.text: Unlocks after the fourth Robot Master clear, whichever boss is fourth. Use it for gaps when a safe landing is available.

stages.name: Fuse Man
stages.tip: Use Bounce Ball and switch on Speed Gear briefly during his fast electric rushes.

stages.name: Tundra Man
stages.tip: Send thunder across the floor and walls. Stay clear of his skating passes and use short jumps on ice.

stages.name: Torch Man
stages.tip: Use Tundra Storm in range. In the stage, Speed Gear gives time to cross the pursuing fire; Tundra Storm can extinguish it.

stages.name: Blast Man
stages.tip: Burn through the bombs with Blazing Torch. Ordinary shots can trigger stage explosives, so check the ground before firing.

returnIntro: Collect the listed utility items before entering the fortress. Ordinary energy, lives and tanks are consumable supplies, not X-style permanent health upgrades.
completionText: Clear all Robot Masters, check the utility items listed above, and refill the weapons needed for the final stages.
features: Use short bursts for hazards and fast attacks. Turning it off between jumps lets the heat fall.
Stronger shots cost more weapon energy. Use it when the extra damage will connect, not while a boss is invulnerable.
Auto-Charge, cooling and recovery parts make a first run more forgiving. Read each effect and disable any part that changes controls in a way you dislike.

sections.title: Shop upgrades and unlocks
paragraphs: Buy Energy Balancer to direct weapon refills, then Energy Balancer Neo if you want a refill to spread across weapons. Auto-Charge lets you focus on movement. Cooling System improves the gear’s recovery.

Buster Plus unlocks after 500 ordinary Buster shots (250 on Newcomer). Cooling System requires 100 gear activations (50 on Newcomer); Speed Gear Booster requires 50 Speed Gear activations (25 on Newcomer).

Power Shield unlocks after 200 total damage (100 on Newcomer). Pierce Protector unlocks after five spike deaths; Energy Catcher after ten Game Overs. These are recovery aids, not goals worth deliberately dying for.
Capsule Catcher requires emptying a special-weapon or Rush meter 30 times. Screw Catcher appears on Saturdays. After beating Wily, Awakener Chip and Cooling System Infinity become available.

E-Tank restores health, W-Tank restores weapons, M-Tank restores both. Stock them before entering the Gear Fortress. Ordinary bolts can be gathered on repeat stage visits; there is no Mega Man 8-style fixed limit.

sections.title: Gear Fortress
paragraphs: Yellow Devil MK-III: use Speed Gear to read the traveling blocks and Chain Blast on the exposed eye. Against Mawverne, avoid the platform edges and attack the exposed target with Bounce Ball.
Reuse the weakness chain in the rematches. Against Wily Machine, use Acid Barrier and attack the exposed target after avoiding the moving machinery.
Wily Machine, second form: use Scramble Thunder while reading the gear-enhanced attacks. Keep heat under control and use tanks from the menu before a lethal hit.

sections.title: Useful tips
paragraphs: Speed Gear helps you learn a room, but does not grant invincibility. Switch it off on safe ground to cool down.
On a failed attempt, buy a useful part or study one hazard before returning. Extra equipment is a normal part of the game.
